_comment: The CLOSED list of data-residency zones and compliance credentials that may appear
on a sheet. The agent SELECTS from this file - it never writes a credential of its
own. scripts/validate.py enforces that: a pill whose text is not in this file
brand/COMPLIANCE.md explains which to pick for a given recipient.

how: Compiled from web search. box.com, box.com/trust and Box's CDN are all blocked
by the build environment's egress policy, so nothing here was read from Box
directly. The zone list agreed across three independent results and is dated
June/July 2026; the certification list is corroborated but less precisely dated.
CONFIRM AGAINST box.com/trust AND box.com/zones BEFORE FIRST CUSTOMER USE.
_verification.recheck: Certification scope and zone coverage both change. Re-verify quarterly.

residencyZones.label: EU data residency
residencyZones.note: Germany and the Netherlands are served by the EU Zone - there is no dedicated zone for either.

residencyZones.label: France data residency
residencyZones.note: In-region compute as well as storage.

residencyZones.label: Canada data residency
residencyZones.note: In-region compute as well as storage.

_zonesNote: Ten zones, and that is the whole list. A country not named above is NOT a zone -
route it to EU or US and say which. Never write a residency claim for a country
All ten are included at no extra cost on Enterprise Plus and Enterprise Advanced.

certifications.label: ISO 27001
certifications.note: Information security management. The backbone of Box's ISMS.

certifications.label: ISO 27018
certifications.note: Protection of personal data in the cloud. Strong alongside GDPR.

certifications.label: SOC 2 Type II
certifications.note: Independent controls report. Ask most security reviewers what they want and this is it.

certifications.label: SOC 1 Type II
certifications.note: SSAE 18. For controls relevant to financial reporting.

certifications.label: GDPR
certifications.note: A regulation Box supports compliance with, not a certification. Fine on a pill; do not call it a certification in copy.

certifications.label: HIPAA / HITECH
certifications.note: US healthcare. Box will sign a BAA.

certifications.label: FINRA / SEC 17a-4
certifications.note: Broker-dealer record retention. The one that matters in US financial services.

certifications.label: FedRAMP High
certifications.note: US federal. Do not offer it to a commercial buyer - it means nothing to them.

certifications.label: C5
certifications.note: German BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Controls Catalogue.

_notConfirmedNote: These could NOT be confirmed from the sources available. Their absence here is
not evidence Box lacks them - only that nobody has checked. Do not put any of
them on a sheet until someone has verified it and moved it into certifications.

assurances.title: Your keys, not ours
assurances.body: Bring your own encryption keys through AWS or Google KMS, including HSM. Box never sees them, and every use is logged.
assurances.verified: Box KeySafe supports AWS KMS, GCP KMS and both platforms' HSM. 'Box never sees or accesses customer managed encryption keys, and no keys are held in memory.' Key usage log is immutable.
assurances.useWhen: Regulated buyers, financial services, anyone whose security review asks who holds the keys. Often the single unlock for a conservative reviewer.

assurances.title: AI that doesn't learn from you
assurances.body: Your content is never used to train AI models. During a request it stays in memory and is never written to disk.
assurances.verified: Box AI Principles: Box will not train AI models on customer content without explicit approval. Neither questions, answers nor document contents are inputs for training third-party LLMs. Content is held in memory for the duration of the request (typically under 60 seconds) and never written to disk.
assurances.useWhen: Almost always. On a sheet whose whole argument is Content + AI, this is the question that stalls the deal if it goes unanswered.

assurances.title: You know which model ran
assurances.body: Box discloses the foundation models behind every Box AI feature.
assurances.verified: Box commits to transparency of AI models and states which are used; Box AI draws on foundation models from multiple vendors including Microsoft Azure and Google.
assurances.useWhen: Where the buyer has an AI governance function, or has asked about model provenance.

_assurancesNote: Short statements that answer what a certification cannot: who holds the keys, and
what happens to content when AI touches it. Rendered as an 'assurances' block under
the compliance pills. Two is usually right; three if the sidebar has room.
Wording is pre-approved - use it verbatim. The validator checks it, same as pills.

worthVerifying.why: A concrete availability number is compelling and easy to check against. Could not confirm Box's figure - do not state one until someone has.

worthVerifying.claim: Sub-processor list, DPA and Standard Contractual Clauses
worthVerifying.why: The first thing a UK/EU privacy lead asks after residency. Box will have these; the wording needs sourcing.
'You can get your content out' defuses lock-in objections. Needs an accurate description of the mechanism.
Routine on security questionnaires. Worth a line if there is a public commitment.
Frequently mandatory for public sector and higher education bids.

_worthVerifyingNote: Candidates that would strengthen this section but could NOT be confirmed from the
sources available. Verify internally, then move into assurances with the wording
someone has signed off. Do not put any of them on a sheet before that.
